newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi king increases size of consultative council.
newsitem.headline: Saudi king increases size of consultative council.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's King Fahd on Saturday issued a decree increasing the number of delegates on the kingdom's consultative Shura council to 90 from 60, Saudi state television reported.
"The Shura council will be made up of 90 members and one president," it quoted the royal decree as saying.

The council's president, Sheikh Mohammad bin Ibrahim bin Jubair, was quoted earlier by Saudi media as saying the number of members on the appointed council would be increased at the start of the new session beginning on Monday.

King Fahd in 1993 set up the council, the kingdom's first representative body for almost 60 years, and created regional assemblies in 13 provinces, the first steps towards giving Saudis more say in running the country's affairs.
The Shura council and regional asemblies have only consultative powers.
Senior members of the royal family traditionally control the country's administration, occupying many top positions at national and provincial level.
The king promised after the 1990-91 Gulf crisis to introduce political and economic reforms gradually with the aim of modernising the system of government.
King Fahd in January was quoted by Saudi media as saying that the kingdom was examining how to develop political reforms including the Shura council.
